title: Standardize admin-action ledger: compact change-diff format, actor/target enrichment, and retention tiers
creator: Miranda Patel
description:
Problem: Our current admin/audit logging lacks a compact, forward-compatible ledger format that captures who did what to which object, why, and the minimal representation of the change. Team feedback shows large event payloads, inconsistent actor/target shapes, and no clear policy for redaction, sampling, or retention across regulated customers.

Goal: Define and adopt a single, compact 'admin-action ledger' schema and encoding for RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML related changes that: 1) encodes the minimal change (delta) in a size-efficient way, 2) standardizes actor and target canonical fields and enrichment anchors, 3) includes provenance (auth method, session id, IP, policy version), 4) supports schema versioning and graceful upgrade, and 5) provides retention/aggregation hints for downstream storage and compliance tiers.

Scope: Example admin actions include role grants/revokes, policy updates, SAML identity mapping changes, organization-level settings, and service-account key rotations. This ticket covers schema, example encodings, redaction rules, read/query hints, and ops guidance for ingestion/retention. Implementation (ingestion library, storage changes) will be follow-up tickets.

Non-goals: Storage backend choices, full immutability migration, or UI changes to Console (those will be separate deliverables).
acceptance_criteria: A canonical ledger schema (v1) is agreed and documented with field descriptions and types
Minimal-change diff encoding defined with examples for common admin ops (grant, revoke, update, rotate)
Actor and target canonicalization rules defined (IDs, external_id, identity_provider, display_hint) and enrichment anchors specified
Redaction and sampling policy documented (sensitive keys, max inline size, fallback to secure blob) and flagged for security review
Retention tiers and a per-event storage hint field defined (tier: short/standard/long) and recommended retention durations
Integration checklist for runtime teams to emit v1 ledger events and migration plan for v0 events
design_notes: We prefer a compact JSONL-first encoding (newline-delimited JSON) for human debugging, but with an option to store diffs as base64-compressed blobs when payload > 16KB to avoid index skew.

Adopt a 'delta-ops' vocabulary inspired by JSON Patch but tightened to our domain: ops = [add, remove, replace, meta] with canonical paths (dot notation) and typed values to avoid ambiguity across services.
Actor identity must be three-part: (principal_type, canonical_id, method_anchor). e.g., principal_type=user canonical_id=usr_12345 method_anchor=saml:okta/<idp-id> or api_key:sa-9876.
Targets (objects) are referenced with stable resource keys: resource_type, resource_id, resource_version(optional). Example: resource_type=rbac_role resource_id=role_aws_admin resource_version=5
Schema must include 'schema_version' at the top-level and 'compatibility' notes for each release to allow consumers to ignore unknown fields safely.

For heavy changes (policy blobs > 8KB) we store a hashed pointer and optional encrypted blob in secure object storage and include a 'payload_ref' with integrity hash so audit queries remain performant.
We will include an optional 'reason' free-text field and require a structured 'approval' block when action originates from an approval flow (approver_id, flow_id, approved_at).
Retention tiers: short (30d), standard (1y), long (7y) with a required 'retention_hint' enum on each event. Regulatory customers may set longer durations via Dedicated/Private configs.
proposed_schema: Top-level v1 fields (text description): ledger_id: string (uuid), occurred_at: rfc3339 timestamp, actor_type: enum(user, service, system), actor_canonical_id: string, actor_anchor: string (idp or api_key), actor_principal_attrs: comma-delimited tags, action_category: enum(admin_role, policy_change, saml_mapping, service_account, org_setting, key_rotation), action_name: string, resource_type: string, resource_id: string, resource_version: string (optional), delta_ops: array of compact op objects, reason: string (optional), approval: string (optional structured blob reference), provenance: string (comma-delimited meta: session_id, src_ip, ua, auth_method), schema_version: "v1", retention_hint: enum(short, standard, long), size_bytes: integer (approx), payload_ref: string (optional pointer to blob storage), trace_ids: comma-delimited, sensitive_redaction: enum(none, partial, full), tags: comma-delimited
redaction_and_sampling: PII and secret material must not be logged inline: keys matching /secret|private_key|credential/ are replaced with '<REDACTED>' unless event marked for full retention in secure tier.

If a single event's serialized size exceeds 16KB, the ingestion library will: 1) replace sensitive fields with redaction markers, 2) extract large blobs to encrypted object storage, and 3) emit a compact event containing payload_ref plus integrity hash.

Sampling: high-frequency machine-originated changes (system/automation actor_type) may be sampled at ingestion with deterministic sampling (hash-based) but must include an aggregated counter event each minute to preserve metrics fidelity.
query_and_indexing_guidance: Index candidates: occurred_at, actor_canonical_id, resource_type+resource_id, action_category, schema_version, retention_hint.
Avoid indexing full 'delta_ops' to keep write amplification down; instead index op-level summaries aggregated into a 'delta_summary' short string (max 256 chars).
Provide a secondary lookup table mapping payload_ref -> event ledger_id for large-blob resolution in secure contexts.
migration_plan_summary: Phase 1 (2 weeks): SDK/library changes to emit v1 schema alongside v0 fields (dual-write), with feature flag controlled rollout to runtime teams.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Consumer-side adapters updated to read v1 and ignore v0, telemetry to measure event sizes and redaction rates.
Phase 3 (4 weeks): Switch ingestion to only accept v1, begin archival/cleanup of v0 events after backup and compatibility window (90 days).
Follow-ups: implement storage-backed payload_ref writer, update retention policy docs, create Console view mapping for ledger events.
